web.markdown:
![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g19/6001_top.jpg)

[Nagano](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6000.html)'s Zenkoji Temple (善光寺, Zenkōji) is one of the most important and popular [temples](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2058.html) in Japan. It was founded in the 7th century and stores the first [Buddhist](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2055.html) statue ever to be brought into Japan when Buddhism was first introduced in the 6th century. The original statue is hidden while a copy of it is shown to the public every six years for a few weeks. The next opportunity to see the statue is in 2027.

The significance of Zenkoji to the development of Nagano was instrumental: many major Japanese cities have evolved either from [castle towns](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2296.html), harbor towns or temple towns. In the case of Nagano, it grew from a temple town which developed around its [temple](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2058.html) of great importance, Zenkoji.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g19/6001_02.jpg)

Niomon Gate

Most recently rebuilt in 1707, Zenkoji's **main hall** is nicely ornamented and contains various [Buddhist](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2055.html) statues. A fee is required to enter the hall's inner chamber, where visitors can take a closer look at the temple's main altar. In the basement of the inner chamber is an **underground passage**, which visitors walk through in complete darkness in search of the "key to paradise". The key is attached to a wall along the corridor and is believed to grant salvation to anybody who touches it.

A short walk behind the main hall stands a relatively recently built pagoda which houses the **Zenkoji History Museum**. The museum showcases a collection of intricately carved statues of different Buddhas and Bodhisattva, allowing one to appreciate up-close the characteristics of each. There is also a display of 100 Rakan, the disciples of Buddha.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g19/6001_03.jpg)

Zenkoji History Museum

South of the main hall is the **Sanmon Gate**, the [temple](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2058.html)'s main gate which dates back to 1750. This designated important cultural property can be entered and houses statues of the Monju Bodhisattva and the four heavenly kings (Shitenno). Its second story offers views of the temple approach.

Just outside the Sanmon Gate stand one large and six medium sized statues of Jizo Bodhisattva. The temple approach leading up to this point is lined with shops selling local specialties and souvenirs, as well as small [restaurants](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2036.html). At the southern end of the approach is **Niomon Gate**, the outer gate of the temple which is guarded by a pair of Nio Guardians.

The many abodes lining the streets parallel to the main [temple](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2058.html) approach indicate just how well received Zenkoji has traditionally been. Today, accommodation at these [temple lodgings](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2025_temple_lodgings.html) (shukubo) is still popular, especially for those who would like to visit the temple at sunrise to participate in its daily morning service (Oasaji). At the service, a solemn ceremony is held, during which visitors receive blessings from a top priest or priestess.

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g19/6001_04.jpg)

Nakamise temple approach viewed from Sanmon Gate

Zenkoji is a ten minute [bus](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2015.html) ride from JR Nagano Station. Alternatively, take a train from the underground Nagaden Nagano Station next to JR Nagano Station and alight at Zenkojishita Station (4 minutes, 170 yen, 2-3 trains per hour), from where it is a 5-10 minute walk to the [temple](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2058.html). Good walkers can reach the temple in about half an hour from Nagano Station.

[How to get to and around Nagano](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e6003.html)

![](https://www.japan-guide.com/g7/6000_map_02.gif)

### Main Hall

#### Hours

From about one hour before sunrise to 16:30 (until 16:00 from December to February, until 16:15 in March and November); the history museum opens from 9:00 to 16:00.

#### Closed

No closing days

#### Admission

600 yen (inner chamber, underground passage and history museum)

Entry to the outer chamber of the main hall is free of charge.

### Sanmon Gate

#### Hours

9:00 to 16:00

#### Closed

No closing days

#### Admission

600 yen

[Share](https://www.linkedin.com/cws/share?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.travelyesplease.com%2Ftravel-blog-zenkoji-temple-nagano%2F)

Nagano was familiar to me as the host of the 1998 Winter Olympics, but beyond that I didn’t know what there was to see and do besides winter sports.

What I discovered during my one day in Nagano was a pleasant city surrounded by low mountains, with a relaxed vibe that quickly drew me in. It was a place I could experience the best of two worlds- nature and wildlife in the surrounding areas, then culture and history at Zenko-ji Temple, the city’s prime attraction.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## **Nagano- A Temple Town at the Gate of Zenko-ji**

Nagano City is known as a monzen-machi, a town that developed around a temple.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Nagano began in the Nara Period (710-794) as a small settlement built at the entrance of Zenko-ji Temple, growing and evolving until it reached city status in 1897.

The 2 km approach to Zenko-ji Temple (omotesando) is typical of a monzen-machi, lined with lodgings, restaurants, and shops.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

In Nagano’s case, the omotesando (Chuo-dori Street) is an interesting combination of old and new. During the walk to Zenko-ji Temple you’ll see several smaller temples and shrines, stone guideposts and lanterns, and converted storehouses and merchant houses selling food and gifts.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## **History of Zenko-ji Temple**

For 1,400 years Zenko-ji Temple has been a centre of Buddhism in Japan, attracting millions of pilgrims and visitors annually.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Zenko-ji Temple was founded in 642 when Yoshimitsu Honda enshrined one of the first Buddhist images brought to Japan, a statue of Amitabha (Amida), the Buddha of Infinite Light and Life. The Amida Triad is the temple’s principal image but it remains hidden from the public. A replica of the hidden Buddha is shown every 6 years, only for a few weeks.

Zenko-ji is not affiliated with any sects so all branches of Buddhism are welcome to worship here.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## **Visiting Zenko-ji Temple- Inside the Temple Grounds**

I spent a surprising amount of time at Zenko-ji Temple, considering the size of the grounds.

During my visit I admired the two wooden gates, went inside the main hall and rubbed a statue of Obinzuru-sama for good health, watched the ritual ringing of the temple bell, and spent some time chatting with a friendly local who wanted to practice his English.

Here are my favourite points of interest at Zenko-ji Temple.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## **Nioman Gate**

Nioman is the first gate you pass under to enter Zenko-ji Temple. There are two guardian statues, Agyo and Ungyo, standing 4.8 metres tall framing the pathway.

![travelyesplease.com | Tour of Zenko-ji Temple- Nagano, Japan](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## **Nakamise Street**

Nakamise is a stone-paved street leading from Nioman Gate towards Zenko-ji’s main hall. It’s said that 7,777 paving stones were used to make the walkway.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

The street is lined with shops and restaurants where you can try local specialties like oyaki dumplings, miso flavoured ice cream, and soba crepes.

## **Roku Jizo (Six Jizo)**

Across from the pond is a platform of six Jizo statues. Jizo is a guardian deity believed to rescue souls in the six realms: hell, the purgatory of hunger, the purgatory of animal passion, the Asura realm, the human realm, and the heavenly realm.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Jizo are also regarded as the protectors of travellers and children, specifically those that are unborn or who have died at a young age.

## **Sanmon Gate**

Sanmon is Zenko-ji’s main gate. Standing 20 metres tall, Sanmon Gate has a double layered roof, with a second level that’s accessible for worship, or just to get a good view of the temple grounds.

![travelyesplease.com | Tour of Zenko-ji Temple- Nagano, Japan](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## **Incense Burner**

I thought the incense burner at Zenko-ji Temple was really interesting because of the fierce mythical lion on top of it. It looked like it had drool dripping from its mouth!

![travelyesplease.com | Tour of Zenko-ji Temple- Nagano, Japan](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

It’s customary to fan the smoke over your body when visiting a temple, an act believed to ward off illness.

## **Hondo (Main Hall)**

Zenko-ji’s main hall was designated a National Treasure of Japan in 1908. It was rebuilt in 1707 in a Buddhist style typical of the middle Edo Period.

![travelyesplease.com | Tour of Zenko-ji Temple- Nagano, Japan](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Inside there are various Buddhist statues and an ornamented inner temple that you can pay to enter if you want a closer look at the main altar. I didn’t go inside the inner chamber, but in the basement visitors can walk through a pitch-black passageway in search of a key that’s believed to secure entry into paradise for anyone who touches it.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## **Shoro (Bell Tower)**

The bell at Zenko-ji was cast in 1667 and the tower housing it was reconstructed in 1853.

![travelyesplease.com | Tour of Zenko-ji Temple- Nagano, Japan](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Make sure you’re here at the top of the hour (from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm) to see the ringing of the bell. It was chosen as one of the 100 Soundscapes of Japan and even rang in the start of the ‘98 Winter Olympics.

## **Final Thoughts About Zenko-ji Temple and My Visit to Nagano**

Even though Zenko-ji is one of the most popular [temples in Japan](https://www.travelyesplease.com/travel-blog-best-temples-in-japan-to-visit/), it has stayed connected to its religious roots. During my visit I felt a calming air of Buddhist contemplation, which is probably why I was in no hurry to leave.

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

As for Nagano, I felt so content and happy here, even though there was nothing really notable about the city, apart from Zenko-ji Temple. It was simply a nice place and I would return here again to explore more of the surrounding areas.

## **Side Trips From Nagano**

Nagano City makes a great base for exploring some of Nagano Prefecture’s popular tourist attractions. Enjoyable day trips from Nagano include a visit to [Matsumoto Castle](https://www.travelyesplease.com/travel-blog-matsumoto-castle/), and a trip to [Jigokudani Monkey Park](https://www.travelyesplease.com/travel-blog-jigokudani-monkey-park/) to see wild snow monkeys bathing in a hot spring.

## **Tips for Visiting Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple**

**Location:** Nagano is the capital city of Nagano Prefecture in the centrally located [Chubu region of Japan.](https://www.travelyesplease.com/travel-blog-japanese-traditions-trip-chubu-region/)

**Getting to Nagano:** From Tokyo, Nagano is about 80-100 minutes by Shinkansen train. There are multiple trains per hour and the ride is covered by the [Japan Rail Pass](https://www.travelyesplease.com/travel-blog-japan-rail-pass/) (buy the pass [here](https://www.jrailpass.com/?utm_source=aff&utm_medium=cpa&utm_campaign=travelyesplease&affiliate=travelyesplease)).

**Getting to Zenko-ji Temple:** Zenko-ji is an enjoyable and easy 30 minute walk from Nagano Station or a 10 minute bus ride (Zenko-ji Line).

**Zenko-ji Temple Opening Hours and Admission:** Visiting Zenko-ji Temple is free of charge, however there is an admission fee to enter the hall’s inner sanctuary/Naijin (ticket includes the Okaidan crypt passage and Zenkoji History Museum).

- Zenko-ji Temple is open 24 hours but the Hondo (hall) is only accessible from sunrise until 4:00, 4:15, or 4:30 pm depending on the month.
- Confirm current hours and prices [here](https://www.zenkoji.jp/en/guide/).

_Information was updated January 2026, but can change without notice. Please confirm directly with the venue._

![travelyesplease.com | Getting to Know Nagano and Zenko-ji Temple](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20699%20466'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## Tours of Nagano and Zenkoji Temple

Here is a trusted site where you can book tours of [Nagano and the surrounding area](https://www.getyourguide.com/s/?partner_id=BFRSJ00&q=nagano&customerSearch=1&searchSource=2&p=1). These are a few I’ve picked out:

# Zenkoji Temple Travel Guide

[Area-Nagano City Area](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/tag/area-nagano-city-area) ,



[Cities and Towns](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/tag/cities-and-towns) ,



[Temples and Shrines](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/tag/temples-and-shrines)

Stay at a temple lodge, participate in fire ceremonies and explore some of the best that Nagano City has to offer. Here is your all-in-one guide to Zenkoji Temple – Nagano City’s most popular destination.

Updated: 2026-04-17

- [![LINE](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/images/icon-line-color.svg)](https://social-plugins.line.me/lineit/share?url=https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/zenkoji-temple-travel-guide)
- [![X](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/images/icon-x.svg)](http://twitter.com/share?text=Zenkoji%20Temple%20Travel%20Guide&url=https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/zenkoji-temple-travel-guide)
- [![Facebook](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/images/icon-facebook-color.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/zenkoji-temple-travel-guide&t=Zenkoji%20Temple%20Travel%20Guide)

![ABG_9818](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_9818.jpg?width=1200&height=798&name=ABG_9818.jpg)

Zenkoji Temple has long been a popular historic detour with pilgrims traveling from Edo (modern-day Tokyo) to Kyoto along the Nakasendo Trail. Nowadays, the temple is not just a destination for people seeking spiritual services, it is also a must-visit for those visiting Nagano.

Legend says that when Buddhism was first introduced to Japan around 1,500 years ago, the first Buddha statue in Japan arrived along with it. Some did not welcome the new religion with open arms, considering it encroaching on Japan’s native religion of Shintoism, and in the ensuing conflict, the original statue was thrown into a river by the Mononobe clan. Zenkoji’s founder, Yoshimitsu Honda, later rescued it and brought the statue to then Shinano Province (modern-day Nagano Prefecture), where Zenkoji was built in 644. The temple has moved several times since then, but the statue has remained hidden in the temple ever since and is known as one of the oldest Buddhist icons in Japan.

Zenkoji Temple Travel Guide

- [Location and Access](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/zenkoji-temple-travel-guide#page01)
- [When to Visit](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/zenkoji-temple-travel-guide#page02)
- [Things to do around Zenkoji](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/zenkoji-temple-travel-guide#page03)
- [Nearby sightseeing](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/zenkoji-temple-travel-guide#page04)
- [Where to stay](https://www.go-nagano.net/en/trip-idea/zenkoji-temple-travel-guide#page05)

## Location and Access

Located in Nagano City, Zenkoji Temple is accessible on foot or by bus from JR Nagano Station.

### On foot

It’s about a 30-minute walk north from JR Nagano Station.

### By Bus

Catch a bus bound for Zenkoji Temple from Bus Stop #1 in front of the Zenkoji Exit of JR Nagano Station to Zenkoji Daimon Bus Stop. From there, it is approximately 8 minutes on foot to the main hall of Zenkoji.

### By Car

Get off at the Nagano IC Exit of the Joshin-etsu Expressway and drive for about 30 minutes to central Nagano City. Park your car at one of the parking lots around the temple (approx. 500 yen for 2 hours).

## When to Visit

Zenkoji Temple is open throughout the year and can be visited at any time with various seasonal highlights. From mid-April to late April, cherry blossoms bloom around the temple and neighboring Joyama Park. From late June to late July, you can see hydrangeas in the temple garden. Then from mid- to late November, golden gingko and vermillion maple leaves can be seen throughout.

### Events at Zenkoji

![IMG_3015](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/IMG_3015.jpg?width=777&height=583&name=IMG_3015.jpg)Lanterns illuminating Joyama Park during the Nagano Tomyo Lantern Festival

Throughout the year, Zenkoji hosts several events, the most notable of which is the Nagano Tomyo Lantern Festival, commemorating the 1998 Nagano Winter Olympics, held in mid- to late February. During the event, the temple is bathed in the Olympic colors and Joyama Park is decorated with incandescent lanterns.

Held once every six years in spring, Zenkoji Gokaicho is a two-month event where a replica of Zenkoji’s hidden Buddhist icon, said to be the first brought to Japan, is put on display. The next Gokaicho will be held from April 4th to June 19th, 2027.

## Things to do around Zenkoji

In addition to visiting the temple itself, visitors can take part in an array of spiritual traditions, whether it’s joining a morning service, experiencing zazen meditation, or staying in a temple lodge and enjoying authentic shojin ryori cuisine - a staple for Buddhist monks. The street leading up to the temple is also filled with restaurants, souvenir shops and various hands-on cultural activities that allow you to bring home something meaningful from your visit to Zenkoji Temple and Nagano City.

### Visit Zenkoji Temple

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP0423.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP0423.jpg)

The main hall of Zenkoji Temple

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_9227.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_9227.jpg)

Above the wall separating the main hall's _naijin_ and _nainaijin_ areas, glittering, golden statues of 25 Bodhisattvas and 100 Kannon greet visitors to the temple.

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_9210.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_9210.jpg)

Praying at the altar in the _naijin_ area of the temple. Beyond the series of curtains in the distance rests Zenkoji's hidden Buddhist icon.

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_9258.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_9258.jpg)

At the entrance to the main hall is a statue of Binzuru, one of the disciples of Siddharta Gautama and known for his healing powers. Visitors rub the statue where they wish to be healed. Over the years, the statue's facial features have been worn away.

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3
- 4

Walk along the stone-paved street and pass through the splendid Niomon and Sanmon gates on the approach to Zenkoji Temple. The main hall, relocated here in 1707, is one of the largest national treasure wooden halls in all of Eastern Japan.

The dark interior is adorned with statues, large ceremonial drums and gilded, hanging ornaments. A wall with red-painted columns and a motif of golden boddhisatvas separates the sitting space (naijin) from the Buddhist altar. Behind the altar on the leftmost side, several curtains cover the temple’s Buddhist icon.

For a small fee, you can enter the naijin sitting area and descend into the dark corridor of the kaidan meguri. After paying your respects before the altar, take the stairs down to the underground passage located under the main hall. Once inside, you are in complete darkness, only able to move forward by touching the wall beside you. Somewhere along the path, you’ll find the “Key of Enlightenment,” a metal latch fixed directly below the temple’s hidden Buddha statue. Touching the latch is believed to create a direct connection with the hidden Buddha statue of Zenkoji and bring good fortune.

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP0355-Edit.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP0355-Edit.jpg)

The Sanmon gate in front of Zenkoji's main hall

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_9765.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_9765.jpg)

Views of Nakamise-dori Street and the cityscape of Nagano from atop the Sanmon Gate

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP7970.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP7970.jpg)

The Kyozo sutra repository to the left of the main hall

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3

You can also climb up the Sanmon gate for expansive views of Nagano City as well as Zenkoji Temple.

Left of the gate is the Kyozo, a sutra repository that stores a complete collection of 6,771 volumes of Buddhist scriptures. In the center of the room is an octagonal holder full of sutras, weighing about 5 tons. Give it a push and fully rotate it once clockwise and you will receive a blessing akin to reading entire scriptures.

Adults H.S. student E.S. student Toddlers All Buildings 1,200 yen 400 yen 100 yen free Zenkoji Naijin and Kaidan Meguri 600 yen 200 yen 50 yen free Sanmon Gate 600 yen 200 yen 50 yen free Kyozo sutra repository 300 yen 100 yen 50 yen free

### Spiritual Experiences (Zazen, Sutra Copying and Mawarigoma)

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_9608.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_9608.jpg)

Zazen meditation

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_0039.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_0039.jpg)

Sutra copying

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_9323.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_9323.jpg)

The Mawarigoma ritual altar

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_9382.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_9382.jpg)

Throwing a wish into the fire as part of the Mawarigoma ritual

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3
- 4

At the Daikanjin of Zenkoji Temple, you can rid yourself of the stresses of everyday life by relaxing your body and mind through Buddhist meditative experiences like Zazen Meditation, Sutra Copying and Mawarigoma.

#### Zazen Meditation

Also known as seated meditation, Zazen is a Buddhist practice that goes back centuries. You sit inside a tatami-laid hall while monks guide you through posture, breathing, and how to focus your mind and body so you can free yourself from thought.

Towards the end of the zazen session, a monk will come over and firmly tap you three times on each shoulder with a wooden slat called a keisaku, helping you to stay awake and relax your back muscles. After the experience is over, you’ll feel refreshed both physically and mentally, and hopefully, be able to meditate in the zazen style on your own in the future.

\*Although zazen meditation traditionally takes place on large cushions on the floor, chair-seated meditation is also available.

#### Sutra Copying

Another meditative experience at Daikanjin is sutra copying. A monk will guide you step by step through the entire process. It begins with cleansing your body with powdered incense. Then preparing your own ink by grinding charcoal and mixing with water. Finally, let your hand and brush flow in harmony across the paper as you complete the sutra. Once completing two sutras, one is given to the monks of Daikanjin and the other you can take home with you.

#### Mawarigoma

In this short but powerful ritual, Mawarigoma is a fire ceremony where you write your wishes on wooden plaques and place them on a fire. The rising smoke created from the burning wish is said to be carried up to a statue of Fudō Myōō—a deity who protects people against misfortune—so that it can be heard and fulfilled. Listen to the constant rhymical drum beat and the chants of a monk as you cast your wish into the fire.

### Activities near Zenkoji Temple

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_0579.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_0579.jpg)

Bead bracelet-making at Galarie Ren, one of Zenkoji's temple lodges

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2196.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_2196.jpg)

Making matcha tea at the teahouse next to Zenkoji Pudding

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_7601.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_7601.jpg)

Creating a unique spice blend at Yawataya Isogoro

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3

Whether you’re going uphill towards Zenkoji Temple or making your way back down, there’s plenty of charming shops and experiences worth stopping by for along Nakamise Street. Create your very own shichimi spice blend at Yawataya Isogoro, mixing classic ingredients or even inventing your very own. Head to Zenkoji Pudding to take part in a relaxing traditional matcha tea ceremony led by an English-speaking tea master. Make your own oyaki dumplings using local Nagano ingredients at Ogawa no Sho, kneading, filling, and cooking them over a traditional irori hearth. Or how about creating a bracelet inspired by Zenkoji’s Buddhist monk prayer beads at Galarie Ren. Each activity can be done in a short time and is a fun way to interact with locals and the culture they hold.

#### Stay in a Shukubo Temple Lodge and Buddhist Monk Cuisine

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_0420.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_0420.jpg)

The entrance to the Fuchinobo temple lodge

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_0242.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_0242.jpg)

Shojin Ryori cuisine at Fuchinobo

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_0249.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_0249.jpg)

Shojin Ryori cuisine at Fuchinobo

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3

There are a total of 39 shukubo lodges which accommodated pilgrims visiting the temple. Today, many of them welcome all travelers interested in learning more about Zenkoji. You can spend the night in a traditional Japanese tatami room, taste traditional Buddhist cuisine and experience the daily regiments of Buddhist monks.

A highlight of staying at a shukubo is eating freshly prepared shojin ryori. This style of food is standard for Buddhist monks, made without the use of meat, fish, animal products, or even some flavorings such as garlic. Though its description may sound bland, you would be surprised how flavorful it can be—often using seasonal vegetables and unique Japanese ingredients. It is sure to nourish your body and mind while keeping your stomach happy and full. Due to the nature of the cuisine, it is also perfect for vegans and vegetarians alike.

### Get up Early to Partake in the Oasaji Morning Service

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_8885.jpg)Monks chanting sutras as part of the Oasaji morning service at Zenkoji

Held every morning throughout the year, Oasaji Morning Service is a ritual held in the main hall of Zenkoji. The service begins at sunrise, earliest at 5:30 am in July and latest at 7:00 am in January. The morning service is two 30-minute sessions, one held by the Daikanjin and another held by the Daihongan monks. Visitors can sit in the naijin of the main hall to pray in front of the alter as the monks perform their rhythmic chants and prayers.

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_9152.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_9152.jpg)

Receiving the juzu-chodai blessing from the head priestess of Daihongan at the end of the Oasaji service

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_8636.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_8636.jpg)

Receiving the juzu-chodai blessing from the head priest of Daikanjin just before the Oasaji service

Next

- 1
- 2

Furthermore, just before the service begins, grab a spot and kneel down in line in front of the main temple where the head priests of the Daikanjin and Daihongan halls walk on their way to their morning prayers. As they pass by, they touch the heads of visitors with their prayer beads. This ritual is a form of blessing and is known as juzu-chodai.

## Nearby sightseeing

### Togakushi

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2341.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_2341.jpg)

The Zuijinmon Gate along the path to the Togakushi Okusha Shrine

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2368.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_2368.jpg)

Towering cedar trees beyond the Zuijinmon Gate

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_2323.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_2323.jpg)

Mirror-like Kagami Pond

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3

Delve deep into the forests to find a series of five shrines deeply rooted in Japanese mythology. Set in the mountains north of Nagano City, its 400-year-old cedar lined trails up to one of the shrines is a highlight. You can also try delicious locally made Togakushi soba noodles here too.

### Matsushiro

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_4266.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_4266.jpg)

The landscape garden at the Former Sanada Residence

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_4204.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_4204.jpg)

The entrance to Matsushiro Castle Ruins

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/ABG_4290.jpg?width=800&name=ABG_4290.jpg)

The entrance to the Former Sanada Residence

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3

A historical castle town that is located just 30-minutes away by bus. Here you can explore well-preserved streets, take a peek into former samurai residences, visit a WWII Underground Tunnel System or try your hand at martial arts at a samurai academy.

### Obuse

Previous

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP1252.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP1252.jpg)

Walking through central Obuse

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP1265.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP1265.jpg)

Obuse's narrow chestnut path behind merchant houses and sake breweries

![](https://www.go-nagano.net/hs-fs/hubfs/nagano-lp/IMGP1254.jpg?width=800&name=IMGP1254.jpg)

The exterior of Obuse Yoritsuki Ryori Kurabu, a restaurant on the grounds of Masuichi-Ichimura Sake Brewery.

Next

- 1
- 2
- 3

Located east of Nagano City and along the Chikuma River, Obuse is famous for its chestnuts and fruits. Along its idyllic streets, laid with chestnut wood tiles, are museums, patisseries and cafes. The famous ukiyo-e artist Katsushika Hokusai, who created _The Great Wave off Kanagawa_, temporarily stayed here during his later years, and you can see exhibitions of his many works at the Hokusai-kan Museum or his large ceiling painting of a phoenix at nearby Gansho-in Temple.

## Where to stay

From budget-friendly hostels to hot spring hotels and traditional lodgings, there are plenty of accommodations within easy reach of Zenkoji Temple and located close to Nagano Station, making it easy to explore the city’s many restaurants and bars.

### Traditional Accommodations

For a more traditional experience, how about staying at a shukubo temple lodge such as Fuchinobo, where you can enjoy shojin ryori and participate in Buddhist rituals? Or stay at Shimizu Ryokan, a historic inn with a wood interior full of Meiji-period charm and maze-like corridors.

### Accommodations with Hot Springs

After a long day of traveling, nothing feels better than taking a relaxing soak in a hot spring. Dormy Inn hotel is equipped with a natural onsen bath on the top floor and is located near Nagano Station. While at Uruoikan, around a 30-minute walk from Zenkoji, offers tatami rooms and public and private bath options, with a unique brown water caused by the naturally iron-rich fresh spring water.

### Hostels and Guest Houses

For budget conscious travelers, hotels such as Pise Worldtrek and 1166 Backpackers offer affordable dormitories and private rooms, all located near the road leading up to Zenkoji.

The saying goes that everyone should visit Zenkoji at least once in their lifetime, and the temple has long attracted worshippers regardless of religious denomination or social status. Its spacious grounds are dotted with places that reflect its culture of faith, including the National Treasure Main Hall and the nationally designated Important Cultural Property Sanmon Gate. This article introduces Zenkoji Temple, its highlights, and recommended experiences. Read to the end to learn how to make the most of your first visit. ## What Is Zenkoji Temple Like? Located in the heart of Nagano City, Nagano Prefecture, Zenkoji Temple is an ancient temple with a history spanning approximately 1,400 years. The saying goes that everyone should visit Zenkoji at least once in their lifetime. As a temple unaffiliated with any single Buddhist sect, it has long attracted worshippers from all walks of life. Today, it is maintained and administered by two Buddhist institutions: Daikanjin of the Tendai sect and Daihongan of the Jodo sect. Approximately 6 million people visit the temple each year. Its principal image is the Ikko Sanzon Amida Nyorai, an Amida triad sharing one halo and believed to be Japan's oldest Buddhist image. However, because it is an absolute secret Buddha image, it cannot be viewed directly. During the Gokaicho ceremony, a replica known as the Maedachi Honzon is displayed instead. This sense of mystery is another distinctive feature of Zenkoji Temple. The spacious grounds are home to numerous historic structures, including the National Treasure Main Hall, offering visitors a chance to appreciate the temple's architecture and culture. The approach to the temple also features Nakamise Street, lined with restaurants and souvenir shops where visitors can sample the flavors of Shinshu. ![Zenkoji Temple, where history, faith, and architectural beauty come together](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_105507_38fcd408_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple Zenkoji Temple, where history, faith, and architectural beauty come together [See Zenkoji Temple Information and Reviews](https://www.gltjp.com/en/directory/item/11869/) ### History of Zenkoji Temple According to the legends of Zenkoji Temple, its principal image, the Ikko Sanzon Amida Nyorai, was brought to Japan with Buddhism in 552 after traveling from India through the Korean kingdom of Baekje. At the time, however, a conflict arose over whether Japan should accept the new religion of Buddhism. The anti-Buddhist Mononobe clan discarded the image in a canal in Naniwa. Honda Yoshimitsu later recovered the image and brought it back to Shinano Province, now Nagano Prefecture, before enshrining it at its present location in 642. Zenkoji Temple traces its origins to 644, when a temple complex was built by imperial order. The temple was named after Honda Yoshimitsu. It developed as a temple unaffiliated with any single Buddhist sect. During the [Kamakura period](https://www.gltjp.com/en/directory/item/13964/) (1185–1333), it also received strong support from Minamoto no Yoritomo and the Hojo clan. As faith in Zenkoji spread, new temples bearing the Zenkoji name were established throughout Japan, further extending its influence. Zenkoji remains one of Nagano's most prominent temples, welcoming many worshippers while preserving its long history and culture of faith. ![Zenkoji Temple has a history spanning approximately 1,400 years](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_105558_911d3ac7_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple Zenkoji Temple has a history spanning approximately 1,400 years ## How to Get to Zenkoji Temple The nearest station to Zenkoji Temple is JR Nagano Station. It takes approximately 30 minutes to walk from the station while taking in the city streets. If you are short on time, a taxi takes approximately 10 minutes. Zenkoji Temple also has paid Parking Lots 1, 3, and 4 for general visitors, making it possible to visit by rental car. Admission Fees Scroll sideways to see more | Area or Ticket Type | Adults | Junior High and High School Students | Elementary School Students | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Main Hall Inner Sanctuary and Okaidan Meguri | ¥800 | ¥300 | ¥100 | | Sanmon Gate | ¥800 | ¥300 | ¥100 | | Sutra Repository | ¥500 | ¥300 | ¥100 | | Combination Ticket (the three areas above plus the Museum) | ¥1,500 | ¥600 | ¥200 | Admission is free for preschool children. ## 5 Highlights of Zenkoji Temple's History and Culture Here are five highlights of Zenkoji Temple. Each offers insight into the culture of faith cultivated over the temple's long history. They include distinctive architecture, panoramic views, and Buddhist images, as well as several hands-on experiences. Use this guide to explore the many sides of Zenkoji Temple. ### 1\. The National Treasure Main Hall The Main Hall, one of the largest wooden National Treasure structures in eastern Japan, is one of Zenkoji Temple's essential highlights. The present hall was rebuilt in 1707 with 108 pillars, said to represent the number of worldly desires. It features a distinctive architectural style known as shumoku-zukuri. Viewed from above, its T-shaped roof ridge resembles a shumoku, the wooden mallet used to strike a temple bell, which is the origin of the style's name. Its interior layout is also symbolic, with the entrance representing the secular world and the innermost area representing the Pure Land. The outer sanctuary contains an image of Enma, the king who judges humanity. The inner sanctuary houses Maitreya and Jizo, saviors of the secular world, while the principal image, the Ikko Sanzon Amida Nyorai, is enshrined on the innermost Ruridan altar. See for yourself the beauty of this solemn wooden structure and the weight of the faith passed down through generations. ![Viewed from above, the Main Hall's roof ridge reveals the shape that gave the shumoku-zukuri style its name](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_112021_71de35c7_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple Viewed from above, the Main Hall's roof ridge reveals the shape that gave the shumoku-zukuri style its name ### 2\. The Sanmon Gate, Offering Panoramic Views of Nagano City The Sanmon Gate, a nationally designated Important Cultural Property, rises directly in front of the Main Hall. Extensive restoration work was carried out from 2002 to 2007, restoring its tochibuki wooden-shingle roof to its original appearance when the gate was built in 1750. One feature to look for is the plaque displaying the three Japanese characters for Zenkoji on the upper level. Five doves are hidden within the characters, earning it the nickname “Dove Character Plaque.” The first character, meaning “good,” is also said to resemble a cow's face. Visitors can climb to the upper level, where the gallery offers panoramic views of the temple grounds and central Nagano City. Climbing a gate normally viewed only from below also provides a rare opportunity to see its historic architecture up close. ![The view south from the Sanmon Gate, overlooking the approach to Zenkoji Temple and Nagano City](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_112140_8281ccb0_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple The view south from the Sanmon Gate, overlooking the approach to Zenkoji Temple and Nagano City ### 3\. The Sutra Repository, Where One Turn Is Said to Bring Merit The Sutra Repository, a nationally designated Important Cultural Property, is a square hall built in 1759 and measuring five bays on each side. At its center stands an enormous octagonal rotating sutra cabinet known as a rinzo, containing all 6,771 volumes of the Issaikyo, a comprehensive collection of Buddhist scriptures. Visitors can touch the rotating cabinet and push it around themselves. It is said that turning it once clockwise brings the same merit as reading the entire Issaikyo collection. Pushing the impressively heavy rinzo around is a special experience found only at Zenkoji Temple. The hall also enshrines statues of Fu Daishi and the Buddhist masters Dengyo and Jikaku, providing another opportunity to explore Buddhist culture. ![Visitors can turn the rinzo themselves, an unusual feature for an Important Cultural Property](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_112209_40bc5dac_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple Visitors can turn the rinzo themselves, an unusual feature for an Important Cultural Property ### 4\. Binzuru, the Statue Touched While Making a Wish The first figure to catch the eye upon entering the Main Hall's outer sanctuary is Binzuru, one of the Sixteen Arhats and a disciple of the Buddha renowned for his supernatural powers. Also known as the “Touching Buddha,” the statue is associated with a tradition in which worshippers touch the same part of the figure as the area of their own body that is unwell in hopes of healing it. Since the statue was enshrined in 1713, countless people have touched it over more than 300 years. Its surface has become so worn that its original facial features can no longer be recognized. Its appearance is itself a historical testament to the depth of people's faith. ![Binzuru is enshrined in the Main Hall's outer sanctuary, based on a tale in which he was instructed to save the people](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_112239_7b0a6504_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple Binzuru is enshrined in the Main Hall's outer sanctuary, based on a tale in which he was instructed to save the people ### 5\. Daikanjin, the Head Temple of the Tendai Sect Located in front of the Sanmon Gate, Daikanjin is the head temple of the Tendai sect at Zenkoji. It oversees 25 subsidiary temples within the Zenkoji complex. Its chief priest, known as the kansu, also serves as a chief priest of Zenkoji Temple, making this an important position. Its history dates back to the time of the temple's founder, Honda Yoshimitsu. Successive generations have served the Zenkoji Nyorai while teaching the public and maintaining the temple. The grounds contain numerous places of interest, including Manzendo Hall, Muryoju-den Hall, Shiunkaku Hall, and a treasure museum. Fudodo Hall in particular holds goma fire rituals, attracting worshippers praying for protection from misfortune and safety for their families. Experiences such as sutra copying and Zen meditation are also available, offering another way to explore Buddhist culture during your visit. ![Daikanjin, the head temple of the Tendai sect at Zenkoji](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_112312_64bfa544_w1920.webp) Daikanjin, the head temple of the Tendai sect at Zenkoji ![Those interested can join a sutra-copying session and transcribe the scripture one character at a time](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_112329_54703691_w1920.webp) Those interested can join a sutra-copying session and transcribe the scripture one character at a time ## Memorable Experiences at Zenkoji Temple Zenkoji Temple offers more than historic buildings to explore. Directly experiencing its long-standing traditions can deepen your understanding and make your visit more meaningful. Here are five recommended experiences that can leave a lasting impression. Each has its own character, so try whichever ones interest you. ### Form a Bond in the Darkness on the Okaidan Meguri One of the defining experiences of a visit to Zenkoji is the Okaidan Meguri, a walk through a pitch-dark passage approximately 148 feet long beneath the principal image. The passage is completely dark, creating a distinctive experience as visitors carefully feel their way forward. Moving through a world without light and relying only on your hands produces a mysterious sensation rarely encountered in everyday life. Along the way is the “Key to the Pure Land,” said to correspond to the lock of the chamber containing the absolute secret Buddha image. Touching it is believed to form a direct bond with the principal image and grant the promise of rebirth in the Pure Land. ![Although it takes only a few minutes, the Okaidan Meguri offers an extraordinary experience in complete darkness](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_112421_e39c5caf_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple Although it takes only a few minutes, the Okaidan Meguri offers an extraordinary experience in complete darkness ### Collect Goshuin as Mementos of Your Trip Collecting goshuin temple stamps as mementos of your visit is another recommended activity. In addition to the standard goshuin bearing the name Zenkoji, limited-edition stamps are available only to visitors who worship at specific structures such as the Main Hall, Sanmon Gate, and Niomon Gate. Each features a different design. When placed together, the stamps form a single picture depicting the Zenkoji Temple grounds. This creates an enjoyable way to explore the grounds while collecting the stamps one by one. There are also many designs closely associated with Zenkoji, including special Binzuru and “Led by a Cow to Zenkoji” goshuin. ![Zenkoji Temple's signature standard goshuin](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_112457_a65a958b_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple Zenkoji Temple's signature standard goshuin ### Sample Shinshu Cuisine on Nakamise Street Nakamise Street stretches along the temple approach and is lined with restaurants and souvenir shops, attracting many visitors before and after worship. Its appeal lies in discovering Nagano's local flavors and products while taking in its traditional atmosphere. One recommended specialty is oyaki, a traditional Shinshu dish. These simple dumplings are made by wrapping seasoned vegetables and wild mountain plants in wheat or buckwheat dough. They come with a variety of fillings, including the classic nozawana pickled greens, and each shop offers its own distinctive variations. The stone-paved approach leading to the Main Hall is also said to contain approximately 7,777 stones, creating another characteristic Zenkoji scene. ![In addition to worshipping, sample Shinshu cuisine and shop on Nakamise Street](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_112605_82f77317_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple In addition to worshipping, sample Shinshu cuisine and shop on Nakamise Street ### The Morning Traditions of Oasaji and Ojuzu Chodai Oasaji is a morning service that begins in the Main Hall at sunrise and is attended by all of Zenkoji Temple's monks. Monks of the Tendai and Jodo sects conduct the service in succession every day of the year, offering a firsthand sense of the faith passed down throughout Zenkoji's long history. It is also a rare opportunity to see the Ruridan altar and the shrine containing the principal image when the normally closed curtain is raised. Another special experience is Ojuzu Chodai, in which a Zenkoji chief priest gently touches worshippers' heads with prayer beads to bestow merit. It is considered a form of teaching through physical action that conveys the Buddhist path without words. No special application is required, and anyone may participate. If your schedule allows, listen to the monks' chanting in the quiet temple grounds early in the morning. ![Oasaji is held every day of the year](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_130412_cdd58f77_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple Oasaji is held every day of the year ### A Temple Lodging Experience Unique to Zenkoji The Zenkoji Temple grounds are home to 39 shukubo, temple lodgings that accommodate worshippers. Each has its own peaceful atmosphere and character, shaped by generations of tradition, as well as thoughtfully prepared temple cuisine. In addition to offering an experience unlike a conventional hotel stay, each lodging has a certified guide who accompanies guests to the next morning's Oasaji service. This provides a special way to attend the solemn early-morning service in the Main Hall and experience the temple's culture of faith more closely. A stay can refresh both mind and body while making your visit even more memorable, so consider spending the night if you are interested. ![Genshoin, a temple lodging on Honen Street in the southeastern area](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_130505_a9346acc_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple Genshoin, a temple lodging on Honen Street in the southeastern area ## Zenkoji Gokaicho: A Grand Ceremony Held Once Every Seven Years Zenkoji Gokaicho is a grand ceremony held only once every seven years according to traditional Japanese counting. It is a special opportunity to worship the Maedachi Honzon, a replica of the principal image that normally remains an absolute secret Buddha. The main highlight is the Eko Pillar, approximately 33 feet tall, erected in front of the Main Hall. A cord known as the “Cord of Goodness” extends from the right hand of the Maedachi Honzon. Touching the pillar is said to form a direct bond with the image. During the event, major Buddhist services are also conducted by the Tendai and Jodo sects, giving the temple grounds a solemn atmosphere unlike that of an ordinary visit. The next Gokaicho will be held for 77 days, from April 4 to June 19, 2027. As this opportunity may not come many times in a lifetime, consider planning a visit during the ceremony. ![A special Gokaicho goshuin offered during the previous ceremony](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_205154_4c50ce2d_w1920.webp) ©Zenkoji Temple A special Gokaicho goshuin offered during the previous ceremony ## 3 Popular Attractions Near Zenkoji Temple Here are three popular attractions near Zenkoji Temple. Each offers a different way to experience Nagano City, from viewing art and taking a walk to shopping. They are easy to combine with a temple visit, so use them as inspiration when planning your sightseeing itinerary. ### 1\. Nagano Prefectural Art Museum The museum houses and exhibits more than 5,500 works, including a valuable collection donated by Japanese-style painter [Higashiyama](https://www.gltjp.com/en/summary/area/gion-higashiyama-yamashina/) Kaii (1908–1999), who frequently depicted the landscapes of Shinshu, as well as works by local artists and paintings of the region's scenery. Its bright, open design faces the park and blends into the surrounding scenery, earning it recognition as a “landscape museum.” When the main building was rebuilt in 2021, the institution was renamed the [Nagano Prefectural Art Museum](https://www.gltjp.com/en/directory/item/12898/) from the Nagano Prefectural Shinano Art Museum, and the Higashiyama Kaii Gallery was also renovated. ![The glass-fronted main building is designed to create a seamless connection between its interior and exterior](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_131545_f2d4059f_w1920.webp) The glass-fronted main building is designed to create a seamless connection between its interior and exterior Name in Japanese 長野県立美術館 Postal Code 380-0801 Address 1-4-4 Hakoshimizu, Nagano City, Nagano [Google Maps](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=%E9%95%B7%E9%87%8E%E7%9C%8C%E7%AB%8B%E7%BE%8E%E8%A1%93%E9%A4%A8%2C1-4-4%20Hakoshimizu%2C%20Nagano%20City%2C%20Nagano) Telephone 026-232-0052 Closed Wednesdays and New Year holidays Business Hours 9:00am - 5:00pm (Admission allowed until 4:30pm) Admission Varies depending on exhibitions The Collection Exhibition (Valid for the Main Hall and Higashiyama Kaii Museum): 700 yen (College student and Age 75 or older 500 yen, High school student and Age 18 or younger: Free) Directions From Nagano Electric Railway’s Zenkojishita Station, walk 11 min. Credit Cards Accepted Official Website[Official Website (Japanese)](https://nagano.art.museum/) [See Nagano Prefectural Art Museum Information and Reviews](https://www.gltjp.com/en/directory/item/12898/) ### 2\. Joyama Park This park spreads across elevated land in Matsumoto City, Nagano Prefecture, and is known for its panoramic views of the Northern Japanese Alps and central Matsumoto. Its origins date to 1842, when Matsumoto feudal lord Toda Mitsutsune planted cherry and maple trees at the ruins of Inukai Castle and opened the grounds to local residents. In 1875, it became the first site in Nagano Prefecture to be officially designated as a park. The approximately 15-acre grounds feature walking paths, a lawn, and an observation deck. In spring, the park attracts many visitors as a renowned cherry blossom viewing destination. ![Many people visit in spring to see the park's famous cherry blossoms](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_131654_fd4e64dd_w1920.webp) Many people visit in spring to see the park's famous cherry blossoms Name in Japanese 城山公園 Postal Code 380-0801 Address 1219 Oaza Arigasaki, Matsumoto, Nagano Prefecture [Google Maps](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=%E5%9F%8E%E5%B1%B1%E5%85%AC%E5%9C%92%2C1219%20Oaza%20Arigasaki%2C%20Matsumoto%2C%20Nagano%20Prefecture) Phone 0263-34-3292 (Matsumoto City Cultural Properties Division) Closed on Open for walking at all times Hours Open for walking at all times Admission Free Access About 8 minutes by car from JR Kita-Matsumoto Station Official website[Official website (Japanese)](https://www.city.matsumoto.nagano.jp/soshiki/134/3977.html) [See Joyama Park Information and Reviews](https://www.gltjp.com/en/directory/item/19018/) ### 3\. Yawataya Isogoro Main Store Yawataya Isogoro operates its main store in Daimoncho, at the foot of the historic Zenkoji Temple in Nagano City, Nagano Prefecture. This specialty spice shop has a history spanning 280 years and sells various blends of shichimi and ichimi chili pepper, including its signature Shichimi Togarashi, available since the company's founding. The store's signature Shichimi Togarashi combines chili pepper with ginger, shiso, Japanese pepper, dried citrus peel, sesame, and hemp seeds. Seasoned using seven ingredients and a distinctive method that has remained unchanged for generations, this long-selling product balances a rich aroma with noticeable heat and has fans throughout Japan. ![The 14 g can features a large chili pepper illustration, with Zenkoji Temple depicted on the other side](https://static.gltjp.com/glt/data/article/22000/21587/20261005_131734_ae56074c_w1920.webp) The 14 g can features a large chili pepper illustration, with Zenkoji Temple depicted on the other side Product name in Japanese 根元 八幡屋礒五郎「七味唐からし」 Manufacturer KONGEN Yawataya Isogoro Price Can (14g) 432 yen; Medium can (28g) 842 yen; Bottle (12g) 454 yen; Bag (8g) 238yen; Bag (18g) 410 yen; Bag (35g) 648 yen; Single-use size (0.2g) x 12 bags 194 yen Sales Locations KONGEN Yawataya Isogoro stores, etc. Official Website[Official Website (English)](https://www.yawataya.co.jp/en/index.php) [See Information and Reviews for Yawataya Isogoro Shichimi Togarashi](https://www.gltjp.com/en/directory/item/11784/) ## Suggested Zenkoji Temple Itinerary Based on the attractions introduced above, the following suggested itinerary provides an efficient way to see Zenkoji Temple's main highlights. A Approximately 2 hours is enough to see the main highlights. Allow around 3 hours if you prefer to explore at a leisurely pace. Q Is there an admission fee for Zenkoji Temple? A Entering the temple grounds is free, but separate admission fees apply to areas such as the Main Hall's inner sanctuary, the Okaidan Meguri, and the Sutra Repository. Q When will the next Gokaicho ceremony be held? A It will be held for 77 days, from Sunday, April 4 to Saturday, June 19, 2027. ## Summary This article has introduced essential information about Zenkoji Temple, its highlights, and a suggested sightseeing itinerary. A source of spiritual support for many people since its founding, Zenkoji is one of Nagano's leading landmarks and continues to preserve its culture of faith. # Zenkoji Temple

__

Trip Moment for Zenkoji Temple Yakuoin shared by Travel Master Maam JourneyPosted 30 days ago, helping 74 travelers with their tripsThere are also 20 other Trip Moments about Zenkoji Temple Yakuoin that can provide additional references for your trip

#Get a discount without relying on luck #Zenkoji Temple is a temple that is a symbol of Nagano. It is important in the history of Buddhism in Japan. It is a temple that many people say "You must go once in your life" and I got it.

The atmosphere inside the temple has a main hall, Sanmon Gate is considered the main gate of the temple, and there are 6 Jizo statues near Sanmo Gate.

The day I went, it was snowing lightly, but I didn't give up on going to worship. The inside is very beautiful and magnificent. When I finished worshiping and walked out, I saw that this place was surrounded by mountains.

#Travel
Take the bus in front of JR Nagano Station. There will be an Alpico Kotsu Bus stop. Get off at Zenkoji Daimon stop. It takes 15 minutes, about 5 stops, and then walk for another 5 minutes.

Before reaching the temple, there will be an area of ​​Nakamise Street. (Nakamise-dori Street) which stretches to the front of the temple is also a street lined with many shops where you can stop by to buy delicious food and enjoy walking around.

🕰️ Opening hours: The main hall closes at 4:30 p.m. Other areas are open 24 hours a day.

Its starting time is adjusted one minute a day according to the sunrise. In the left chart, … - During the term of the line goes down towards left: The schedule is adjusted a minute earlier each day - During the term of the line goes down towards right: The schedule is adjusted a minute later each day The **Rosary Blessing O-JUZU CHODAI** takes place 4 times a day while the Abbot and the Abbess come up to the HONDO for the O-ASAJI and go down. The first once takes place slightly earlier than O-ASAJI schedule. However, the schedule of following 3 times are not fixed, depend on the application status of the prayers. Anybody can join this O-JUZU CHODAI. Please visit at the pavement in front of the HONDO a bit earlier than the time when the Abbot or the Abbess passes by and wait for it. Neither booking nor any charge are required. ### Inner Sanctuary Admission Ticket #### An **admission ticket NAIJIN-KEN** is required for entering places below: 1. Zenkoji History Museum in the CHUREIDEN Pagoda #### The NAIJIN-KEN is available at the location below in the temple precincts. - Ticket issuing machine located at your right hand side from the HONDO main entrance - Temple goods booth JUYOHIN-JO just inside the HONDO main entrance - Temple goods office JUYOHIN-JO in front of the HONDO - CHUREIDEN Pagoda entrance NAIJIN-KEN **Distribution Charge** Adults and Students of University & CollegeJPY 800.\_Students in Grades 7-12JPY 300.\_Students in Grades 1-6JPY 100.\_Pre-schoolersFREE You can enter the temple precincts and the Outer Sanctuary GEJIN of the HONDO (the part with floor-board) in free of charge.

Zenko-ji Temple was one of the highlights of our visit to Japan. The temple itself is absolutely stunning, with magnificent architecture, beautiful wooden details, and a peaceful atmosphere that immediately makes you slow down and appreciate your surroundings.

The approach to the temple is equally impressive, lined with traditional shops and filled with a sense of history and spirituality. Despite attracting many visitors, the site never felt overcrowded and retained a calm, respectful ambience.

What struck us most was the feeling of serenity. Whether you are interested in Buddhism, Japanese culture, or simply beautiful places, Zenko-ji offers a memorable experience. The grounds are immaculately maintained, and there is always something fascinating to discover around every corner.

A wonderful place to spend a few hours and one that should not be missed when visiting Nagano.
